collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager claims to know everything already, so a friend makes up a fact: try the made-up fact, or give up the test.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Whatever anyone tells (subject), (subject.he/she) already knew it. The tide's turning early? Knew it. The fish are biting by the rocks? Knew it. (friend) has decided, just this once, to test this. (friend.He/she) has made up a fact.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) decides that would be a little unkind, and tells (subject) a true fact instead: that the eels in the stream are born out in the sea. "Knew it," says (subject). Then, after a moment: "Wait. Really?" (friend) decides this is a victory of sorts.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "Did you know," says (friend), "that crabs walk sideways because they're shy?" "Knew it," says (subject), instantly. Then (subject.he/she) pauses, looks at (friend), and sees the corner of (friend.his/her) mouth twitching. "...I did not know that," (subject) admits, "because it isn't true." They both laugh. (subject) says "knew it" a little less after that. Only a little.
